result_summary: Killed-at-gate. 172 of 574 cross-article insertions (30.0%) have a cheapest cost to the host document above 0.6, and the record requires at least 50%. No convention measured brings the reading to 50% (19.2% and 48.6% by direction, 5.2% on statements of 5+ words, 32.4% with shipped-path ibm hosts, 39.3% per unique statement). The sanity check passed (V 0/24, margin +4.708, d' 4.684). The readings taken after the gate do not decide the verdict: at c=0.60 the ibm panel keeps V 0/24 and margin +4.708 with max |delta smd| 0.0025 and 0/495 triangle violations, and the pooled CV of the increment falls 0.3957 → 0.1189 (70.0%). That fall is produced by inserted statements under 5 words, which the shipped default segmentation returns for the markdown sources (10 of 52 wergeland statements, 28 of 70 ibm statements): their mean cost to the host statements is 1.097 and the cap sets it to 0.603, while statements of 5+ words have 0.544 and 0.53. On statements of 5+ words the CV falls 15.6% (26.6% with the host-length factor removed). The increment SMD(B, B + s) equals the mean cost from the inserted statement to all n host statements divided by n + 1 (closed form checked on all 574 insertions), so the cap changes 511/574 increments while the gate, which takes the cheapest arc, counts 172.
caveats: Conventions fixed in the configuration cell before scoring, where the record leaves a choice: hosts are the 10 base documents of the structure fixture (each of the 7 ibm bases is stored there with its markdown title line as statement 0); inserted statements are every statement the shipped default segmentation returns for the other article's source file (52 wergeland, 70 ibm), markup fragments included; the increment is SMD(B, B + s); the registered CV reading pools all 574 insertions; the 5-word split is a convention of this notebook, not a registered quantity. The kill-gate and the bar measure different arcs: the gate takes the cheapest arc, the increment averages all arcs to the host. acceptance.met is true because the four bar conditions hold as written on the registered reading; the verdict follows the kill-gate, which is decided first. The host-length factor 1/(n + 1) alone has a CV of 0.0847 that no cap changes; on statements of 5+ words a cap leaving only that factor would give a fall of 0.3721, below the bar. One pair of articles, both about artificial intelligence; hosts of 11 to 14 statements.
